quirks: Danish military levy rolls (laegdsruller) begin in 1789 and enroll every male from early childhood under his father's name — each son's entry sits directly beneath the father's, making the rolls DIRECT parentage evidence for a male subject.
Danish naming is patronymic before ~1850: 'Mikkel Nielsen' means Mikkel son of Niels, so the father's given name is Niels — the patronymic alone does not identify which Niels.
Vital events are recorded in parish church books (kirkeboeger); baptism entries name both parents. Civil registration is much later.
The Stagstrup parish register is only ~3% name-indexed on FamilySearch — plan to browse the register images by year rather than rely on the index.

items.description: Robert Eastham Jr.'s mother's birthplace: Virginia (1880 census image, a_144) vs. Kentucky (1870 marriage bond self-report, a_159)
items.independence_analysis: The two assertions draw on distinct record events created by different informants at different times. a_144 is a 1880 census enumeration in which an unknown household member reported Robert's parents' birthplaces to an enumerator; a_159 is Robert's sworn self-declaration on a 1870 marriage bond in which he personally stated his mother was born in Kentucky. The records are independent — neither was copied from the other, and they were created a decade apart. Both ultimately rely on Robert's personal knowledge of his own family origins, but the quality of transmission differs: the census entry is oral statement filtered through an enumerator and recorder, while the bond is Robert's direct written declaration.
items.weighing_analysis: Under GPS evidence-weighing principles, a contemporary sworn self-report on a legal document carries greater weight than a retrospective census entry made by an unknown informant. a_159 (1870 marriage bond) is primary information: Robert personally swore the statement on a legal instrument and is the most proximate source for facts about his own parentage. a_144 (1880 census) is secondary information: the reporter is unknown, the enumeration is retrospective, and census entries for parents' birthplaces are routinely less reliable than sworn legal statements. The bond is also closer in time to the events it describes. Additionally, the a_159 value (Mother=Kentucky) aligns with Polley A.P. Burton's 1880 census parental birthplace record (Mother=Kentucky), corroborating the sibling hypothesis (h_002) that Robert Jr. and Polley Burton share a common Virginia-born father and Kentucky-born mother.
items.resolution_rationale: a_159 (Robert's sworn self-report on the 1870 marriage bond: Mother born Kentucky) is accepted over a_144 (1880 census by unknown informant: Mother born Virginia). Primary sworn self-report on a legal instrument outweighs secondary retrospective census entry by unknown informant.

items.claim: Polly Burton (Mary A. Burton, Polley A.P. Burton) — Jahue B. Burton's wife shown in the 1850–1880 census records in Pulaski County, Kentucky — is a different person from Mary Ann Eastham, who married Ephriam Boggs in Greenup County, Kentucky on 30 January 1844. The FamilySearch profile LYYX-DS1 incorrectly merges these two distinct women.
items.notes: Primary hypothesis for q_001. The Boggs/Eastham marriage record (src_005, a_115) provides direct evidence of a separate Mary Ann Eastham who married Ephriam Boggs on 30 January 1844 in Greenup County — a woman who cannot simultaneously be Jahue Burton's wife Polly in Pulaski County. The 'Father of the Bride' Robert Eastham named in that marriage record (a_117) must have been born approximately 1795-1805 to have a daughter old enough to marry in 1844, making him too old to be the Robert Eastham Jr. (b. ~1822, Greenup County) who co-resided with the Burtons in 1850 and 1860. Four census records consistently name Jahue's wife as Mary A. or Polly Burton but never state an Eastham maiden name, providing negative evidence against the FamilySearch merger. The 1880 census image of the Burton household (log_021) documents Polley A.P. Burton's father as Virginia-born and her mother as Kentucky-born; these facts are recorded in the log entry but no formal assertions have yet been extracted from that image, so no assertion IDs for those parental birthplace facts are available here.

items.claim: Robert Eastham Jr. (b. ~1822, Greenup County, Kentucky; co-resident in the Jahue B. Burton household in Pulaski County in both the 1850 and 1860 censuses; married Margaret Rucker in Boyd County, Kentucky, 25 January 1870) is a sibling of Polley A.P. Burton (Jahue B. Burton's wife), both being children of a Virginia-born Eastham father and a Kentucky-born mother. This accounts for both Polley's possible Eastham maiden name and Robert Jr.'s persistent co-residence with the Burton family.
